question.worked_solution:
If we plug in $x=0$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{8x}-{e}^{5x}-3x}{{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[{e}^{8x}-{e}^{5x}-3x]}^{′}}{[{x}^{2}]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{8{e}^{8x}-5{e}^{5x}-3}{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{8x}-{e}^{5x}-3x}{{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{8{e}^{8x}-5{e}^{5x}-3}{2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[8{e}^{8x}-5{e}^{5x}-3]}^{′}}{[2x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{64{e}^{8x}-25{e}^{5x}}{2} \\  & =\frac{64(1)-25(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{39}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
